title: Exceptions
summary: Throwing and catching exceptions, the common exception types, catch order and exception filters, finally, rethrowing with throw versus throw ex, custom exception classes with inner exceptions, guard clauses and ArgumentException helpers, and when to use Try methods or result types instead.

cards.q: Why should catch (Exception) come after catch (FormatException)?
cards.a:
Catches are tried in order, and Exception would catch everything

The first catch whose type matches handles the exception. `Exception` matches every exception, so a specific catch after it could never run, and the compiler rejects it.

cards.q: What is the difference between throw; and throw e; inside a catch?
cards.a:
throw; rethrows with the original stack trace; throw e; resets the trace to the current line

Both rethrow the same exception, but `throw e;` starts the stack trace again at the catch, hiding where the error really happened.

cards.q: When does a finally block run?
cards.a:
Always, whether or not an exception happened

`finally` runs after the try, after a catch, or while an uncaught exception passes through. It is for clean-up that must happen in every case.
